claims: The Annual Wage Review 2026 "lifted award rates and the National Minimum Wage by ${pct(AWR)}" (renders 4.75%).
whys: The National Minimum Wage rose 5.97% in the 2026 Annual Wage Review. Only modern award minimums rose 4.75%. The sentence gives the NMW the award figure.
constants: lib/constants/minimum-wage.ts NMW_DECISION (add an nmwIncrease field next to awardIncrease)
reviewerNotes: Valid: the answer gives the National Minimum Wage the 4.75% award increase. Per the brief's known-correct facts, the NMW rose 5.97%. The same issue is at line 88. Not changed (no new numbers).

claims: "award-free employees on the National Minimum Wage, got the ${pct(AWR)} increase" (4.75%).
whys: Award-free employees on the NMW got 5.97%, not the 4.75% award increase. The question "Who gets the 4.75% pay increase?" is locked, but this answer should limit the 4.75% to award employees.
constants: lib/constants/minimum-wage.ts NMW_DECISION.awardIncrease vs a new NMW increase constant

claims: "Can a pay rise ... leave me worse off?" is answered "No" (the old closing line said "You always take home more money after a pay rise").
whys: The page's own MLS answer (line 121) says the Medicare Levy Surcharge applies to TOTAL income once you cross the tier 1 threshold. A single with no private hospital cover who gets a small rise just past that threshold takes home less. I narrowed the closing sentence to "On the income tax brackets alone..." but the bare "No" still needs a human decision.

claims: the business name and ABN that must appear on every Australian payslip
whys: Fair Work Regulations require the ABN only if the employer has one. The table on the same page says so ('if the employer has one'), but this list item, the paragraph at line 39 and the FAQ answer at payslip-generator-faqs.ts line 15 say the ABN is required on every payslip.
